options.text: At the melting point, particles vibrate enough to leave fixed positions; that temperature identifies the solid-to-liquid change at atmospheric pressure.
The melting point is the temperature at which liquid ghee turns back into solid ghee while being heated.
Solid ghee melts at that temperature even if particle vibrations do not increase.
Any warm temperature counts as the melting point, not only the fixed temperature where solid becomes liquid.

stem:
The diagram shows Harsh heating solid ghee in a dish. A thermometer is placed in the ghee. At one fixed temperature the solid ghee turns into liquid ghee.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Heating increases particle vibration until particles leave fixed positions; the melting point is that fixed temperature for solid→liquid at atmospheric pressure.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source diagram into heated dish of solid ghee with thermometer.
